profile.behavior: An opportunistic omnivore that swims, dips for aquatic prey, scavenges, and forages on the ground for worms and insects. Often nests colonially and is mainly migratory.
field_marks: Small, slender gull with a rounded head and long wings
White head and underparts; light brown head streaking in nonbreeding plumage
Short, tapered greenish-yellow bill, sometimes with a dusky winter smudge
Dark eye and slender, dull yellow-green legs
Black wingtips with bold white spots; otherwise white tail
profile.habitat: Breeds around wetlands, marshes, meadows, beaches, and other sites near water; winters along coasts and other waterside habitats, often also feeding in fields.

findings: Species identity is correct: the plate labels Common Gull, Larus canus, family Laridae, matching eBird, Wikipedia, and Animal Diversity Web.

The primary specimen is a single complete bird with one head, one beak, two folded wings represented in side view, two legs with webbed feet, and one tail. No duplicate or malformed attached parts are present.
